title: The Story translation procedure
description:
As an editor, I want a published Story translated, checked, polished and published by one procedure, so every enabled language catches up without delaying the English page.

Design: section 3 (registered Tactus procedure `papyrus.story.localize`, one run per Story per language, started only by the plan's desired-state record and by `papyrus stories localize` writing the same record). Parent epic PPY-251157; also serves PPY-376e85 (copy-edit and verify).

Decisions of Ryan 2026-11-13 applied here:
1. The machine may rewrite its own translation, and every rewrite is re-checked against the English source; it never touches wording a person corrected (pinned human blocks stay advice-only).
2. Stages 4 to 6 repeat as a convergence loop on changed blocks only: continue while a round strictly reduces the weighted findings and adds no faithfulness finding; a block whose rewrite makes faithfulness worse reverts. Copy-edit rewriting happens inside this loop, replacing the plan's single re-translation step.
3. Stock phrasing the checks keep finding in a translation is reported back on the English Story as advice for its editor.
4. Target-locale conventions (naming, register, press norms) come through the per-language glossary and pack and never remove or alter a factual claim.
5. A rule drives a rewrite only at about 9 in 10 correct on held-out examples, measured per language; below that it only advises.
6. Spanish and Chinese run through the same procedure from the start.
No paid human reviewer sits anywhere in the procedure; nothing waits for a person.

```gherkin
Feature: A published Story is translated, checked, polished and published by one procedure
  Scenario: A clean Story appears in Chinese after English publish
    Given Simplified Chinese is enabled on the site
    When an editor publishes an English Story
    Then one translation run starts for Chinese
    And the Chinese page is published with the AI-translated label
    And the run records the source version, models, rule versions, findings and cost

  Scenario: The machine polishes its own translation until it converges
    Given the first translation has typography and translationese findings
    When the polish rounds run
    Then each round rewrites only blocks with findings and checks them against the English again
    And the rounds stop when a round changes nothing or no longer reduces the findings
    And the run records the number of rounds

  Scenario: Polishing never changes the facts
    Given the polish step rewrites a sentence and drops "may"
    When the sentence is compared with the English again
    Then the rewrite is discarded and the earlier wording kept
    And the run records one reverted block

  Scenario: Polishing never touches wording a person corrected
    Given a corrector fixed one paragraph of the Chinese page
    When the English Story is republished and the polish rounds run
    Then that paragraph is left exactly as the corrector wrote it
    And findings on it are advice only

  Scenario: Stock phrasing is reported back on the English Story
    Given the Chinese checks keep finding a stock phrase that came from the English Story
    When the run finishes
    Then the English Story's editor sees advice naming the phrase and its place in the English text

  Scenario: A translation that changes a number is held
    Given the translation still says "86%" where the English says "68 percent" after polishing
    Then the Chinese page is not published
    And a review request says which number differs
    And the people subscribed to Chinese translations are told

  Scenario: Running it twice does nothing the second time
    Given a finished translation run for a Story, language and source version
    When the same run is started again
    Then no model is called and no version is saved

  Scenario: Only what changed is translated again
    Given a published Chinese localization
    When the English Story is republished with one paragraph changed
    Then one block is translated
    And a paragraph a corrector fixed is left exactly as they wrote it

  Scenario: An outage stops the run and says so
    Given the judging model cannot be reached
    When a translation run starts
    Then the run fails with that reason
    And nothing is published
    And the next start continues from the finished steps

  Scenario: An editor starts it by hand
    When an editor runs "papyrus stories localize --story L --language zh-Hans"
    Then the same procedure runs as after a publish
    And "--dry-run" prints the blocks, glossary terms and predicted cost and writes nothing
```
